codeReview.summary: The MCP initializer expectation updates are correct, but the web.spec expectation change hard-codes a demonstrably incorrect auth-source outcome instead of fixing the underlying regression noted by the worker.

issues.description: The test was changed to expect `scrapersAuthType` as `SYSTEM_DEFINED`, which codifies the broken behavior in `web.ts` where `isUserProvided` only flips when `contributed` is true (`web.ts` lines 191-203 in this commit snapshot), and `contributed` is only set in the SSRF-block path. This makes USER_PROVIDED unreachable for non-URL user-provided keys like `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY`. The feature scope explicitly allowed implementation correction when demonstrably wrong, so this should have been fixed in implementation rather than updating the expectation.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The backend-migration-worker procedure is too rigid for expectation-drift-only tasks: its "write or update tests first" step doesn't map cleanly when existing tests are the artifact being reconciled.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Handoff `skillFeedback.suggestedChanges` explicitly calls out this mismatch; transcript skeleton shows a reproduce/analyze/edit flow rather than a meaningful tests-first split.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The SSRF hardening side-effect on web auth-source reporting was not captured in shared library notes, forcing commit-history archaeology to determine whether the test or implementation was stale.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Transcript skeleton includes `git diff 1312cd757..9cfdf2ba0 -- packages/api/src/web/web.ts` to infer the regression path; `.factory/library` contains SSRF hardening notes but no specific `loadWebSearchAuth` auth-source semantics note.
